messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 503 spike on /v1/generate (eu-west-1). error rate 12% over 3m, latency p95 1.2s. Pager to @maya. svc: inference-hosted; cluster: euw-prod-1. runbook: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/inference-503

maya: I'm on it, ack. starting live mitigation checklist. grabbing logs now.

ben: seeing the same from synthetic checks. looks like KV cache thrash on gpt-small-1.

maya: quick mitigation: 1) scale up pool by +2 nodes (dedicated burst) 2) route 10% traffic to euw-failover 3) fall back non-critical tenants to gpt-medium-2 quantized. doing step 1 now.

liam: notifying support + customers page with preliminary impact: ~5% of requests failing for some customers, degraded latency for many. @sarah can you collate affected accounts?

sarah: will pull list from telemetry and open a thread to TLs. Initial hit on billing-prod and docs-search customers. I'll DM CSMs.

maya: scaled +2 nodes, autoscaler throttled initially due to scheduling; forced allocation succeeded. error rate dropped to 3% after reroute. keeping watch.

ben: suggestion: enable prefix caching bypass for long-tails (low risk) to reduce KV pressure.

maya: applied prefix bypass, no immediate regressions. monitoring.

incident-bot: Mitigation note: fallback policy active -> gpt-medium-2 (quantized) for non-paying-dev tenants.

julie: nice work. can we capture exact timeline and actions for the post-incident? I can spin up the RCA doc skeleton.

liam: please do. propose we schedule postmortem review tomorrow 1600 UTC. owners: maya (ops timeline + mitigation), ben (telemetry + root cause), julie (writeup editor), ashley (commerce/customer impact + sign-off).

maya: created draft timeline, pushing to docs: https://docs.redwood/company/postmortems/2865004444-incident-draft (private). quick timeline snippet:```
00:00 - alert triggered (503 spike)
00:02 - oncall ack (maya)
00:05 - scale +2 nodes requested
00:08 - forced allocation success
00:12 - reroute 10% to euw-failover
00:20 - fallback policy active for non-critical tenants
00:35 - error rate stable ~2-3%
```

ben: from traces: KV cache eviction rate jumped x6 due to a single tenant sending long-context streams. root cause candidate = unbounded prefix growth + cache churn.

julie: added section headings and an action items table in the doc. action examples: add eviction safety guard (owner: ben, due: 2w), enforce request size limits per tenant (owner: ashley, due: 1w), create better autoscaler fallback (owner: maya, due: 3w).

ashley: I'll coordinate customer comms and legal check for the impacted accounts. flagging as Sev2 for billing team.

liam: scheduled postmortem review: 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC — invite sent to eng, infra, support, legal.

maya: drafting RCA sections: contributing factors, timeline, impact summary, tests to prevent regressions. sharing a quick evidence list in doc.

ben: peer note on draft: expand on "unbounded prefix growth" with a small repro and include logs (I've uploaded traces to s3://incidents/2865004444/traces). also add quant benchmark for fallback model fidelity.

julie: I've cleaned up tone for customer-facing section. changed passive phrasing and made action owners explicit.

ashley: reviewed draft, requested minor edits around SLA wording. once updated I can sign off and we can publish to customer comms.

maya: edits applied. final check from owners please. once we have approvals I'll mark postmortem as complete and create the follow-up issues in Jira (links in doc).

ben: reviewed and :white_check_mark: good from telemetry side. added Jira IDS: INF-4928 (eviction guard), INF-4929 (tenant request caps).

ashley: legal and comms approved. ready to sign-off.

maya: marking RCA as ready and handing off to postmortem queue. closing incident channel. thanks all for fast mitigation and clear owners. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed. Summary: mitigation succeeded, error rate back to baseline. Postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood/company/postmortems/2865004444-incident-draft. Follow-ups tracked: INF-4928, INF-4929, INF-4930 (autoscaler fallback).
